summary.headline: Aadhar Housing Q2 FY27 PAT rose to INR308 crore (vs INR266 crore) with AUM up 18% YoY to INR32,643 crore; credit cost guided to 25 bps for FY.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 showed steady execution: disbursements of INR2,577 crore (+22% YoY) and AUM of INR32,643 crore (+18% reported, ~20% like-to-like after the cheque-clearance accounting change). PAT was INR308 crore against INR266 crore a year earlier, and H1 PAT was INR591 crore. Gross NPA improved to 1.34% from 1.42% YoY, but credit cost of 31 bps in Q2 sat above the 25 bps annual guidance, which management attributed to timing and said it expects to correct by year-end. Management flagged RBI's 25 bps repo hike to 5.5% and rising competition, and said it will protect spreads rather than chase yields.

financial_highlights.value: 31 bps (management also cited 30 bps on the AUM basis in the Q&A)

segments.name: Home loans
segments.commentary: About 73% of AUM; GNPA about 1.0%, up from 1.2% a year earlier as stated on the call.

segments.name: Non-home loans (incl. LAP)
segments.commentary: About 27% of AUM; GNPA about 2.0% (2.01% a year earlier). Disbursement growth recovering from 24% to 26% QoQ, with management targeting about 28% share by year-end.

segments.name: Salaried customers
segments.commentary: 55% of AUM. Average ticket size INR11.3 lakh; LTV about 61%.

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: Uttar Pradesh AUM growth about 9% vs ~18% blended, but disbursement growth about 23% in both UP and Karnataka; management attributed UP's lag to a faster run-down of its older vintage book.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term guidance maintained: 18-20% disbursement growth and 20% AUM and PAT growth (PAT after ESOP cost).
Management expects 20%+ disbursement growth in H2 FY27 and a minimum of 20% in Q3; October run-rate moved from about INR800 crore average to about INR900 crore.
Credit cost guided at 25 bps for the full year, with year-end headline NNPA/GNPA expected at about 1.10-1.15%; FY AUM credit cost about 22-23 bps.
Assignment volume expected at INR2,000-2,050 crore for FY27, vs about INR1,700-1,800 crore in FY26.
Branch additions guided at 40-50 for FY27; about 5-6 added so far with about 40 in pipeline.
Non-home loan share expected to stabilise at about 28% by end FY27; 70:30 home loan to non-home loan mix thereafter.
ESOP charge (granted Jan 2026 at INR425 per share) is front-loaded: about 40% in year one and about 30% in year two of the five-year vesting.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 632 across 23 states and over 555 districts as of Sep 2026; one branch added in Jammu in Q2.
Branch addition guidance of 40-50 for FY27, with about 40 in the pipeline.
Management is building in-house AI platforms for document intelligence, voice intelligence, decisioning, enterprise access and management intelligence.
Employees on roll: 6,112 as of 30 Sep 2026.
demand_pricing: Competition is rising. Industry balance transfer-out runs at about 6.5-7%, while Aadhar's BT-out was 5.1% in Q2, down 40 bps YoY.

Post-RBI repo hike of 25 bps to 5.5%, management said it will protect spreads over chasing yields. Around 75% of both assets and liabilities are floating, and pass-through follows an ALCO decision with up to a one-quarter lag under the RPLR model.
No pass-through decision yet; ALCO expected in Dec/Jan after the RBI policy.

Incremental borrowing at 7.5%. Management cites AA+ ratings from all three agencies (ICRA and India Ratings upgraded in Q2) as cutting NCD costs by about 20 bps on average and opening pension and life insurance funding pools.
Insurance: IRDAI draft guidelines are under industry review; management says fee income and opex levers can offset any impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Stage 2 rise QoQ from about 3.3% to 3.55%, and is there state concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it seasonal with no specific state concentration. September 2026 was comparable to September 2025, and the team is monitoring by market. Analyst noted Q1 to Q2 had moved the other way last year.

qa_highlights.question: How much assignment income was booked and is it rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Net assignment impact (new income less unwinding) was only about INR10 crore higher YoY at PBT level in Q2. FY27 assignment volume is guided at INR2,000-2,050 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How will cost of funds and spreads move in H2 with the rate hike and rating upgrades?
qa_highlights.answer: Spreads should hold to a large extent because around 75% of assets are floating. Any lag is about one quarter, and a rate pass-through decision will follow the December/January ALCO meeting. Rating upgrades are expected to lower NCD costs by about 20 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% PAT guidance before or after ESOP cost, and how long does the ESOP charge last?
qa_highlights.answer: The 20% PAT growth guidance is after ESOP cost. The charge runs over five years, with about 40% in year one and 30% in year two, then declining.

qa_highlights.question: Why is non-home loan growth lagging, and what are the GNPA trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Non-home loan tightening in Q4 FY26 is being reversed, with NHL share moving from 24% to 26% and targeted at about 28% by year-end. HL GNPA is about 1.0% and NHL about 2.0%, against 1.2% and 2.01% a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q3 disbursement outlook and October run-rate, and what is the insurance regulation impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Q3 disbursement growth is guided at a minimum of 20%. October run-rate has risen from about INR800 crore to about INR900 crore per month. On IRDAI draft insurance rules, management is waiting for final guidelines and will use fee and opex levers.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q2 credit cost above the guided range, and what is the year-end target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 credit cost was about 31 bps and that full-year guidance is annual. It expects to end FY27 at 25 bps on AUM average, with headline NPA of 1.10-1.15%.

qa_highlights.question: What was the impact of the cheque-clearance accounting change on disbursement and AUM?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27 disbursement was about INR350 crore lower YoY due to the switch to clearance. In Q2 the effect evened out, so no separate Q2 handover figure was given. Management estimated the old-basis Q2 figure would have been about INR200-250 crore higher.

qa_highlights.question: Why is branch addition slowing and what explains the BT-out rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 40-50 branches for FY27, with about 5-6 added so far and about 40 in the pipeline. BT-out is seasonally low in Q1 and rises in Q2 and Q3; the 5.1% figure is 40 bps lower YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Could NHB outlay increases benefit funding?
qa_highlights.answer: No NHB circular yet on increased outlay; the company is engaging with NHB and signals are positive, but no quantum has been given.

qa_highlights.question: How much LAP exposure is agri-linked and what is 1+ DPD?
qa_highlights.answer: Agri or seasonal income is capped at 25% of a borrower's income under credit policy, with a 55% FOIR applied. 1+ DPD is described as flattish and in a comfortable zone; no specific figure was given.

risks_watch: Stage 2 rose from about 3.3% QoQ to about 3.55%; management calls it seasonal, but the analyst noted Q1 to Q2 moved the other way last year, so track Stage 2 and bounce rates by market next quarter.
Credit cost of 31 bps in Q2 is above the 25 bps full-year guidance; management expects to return to 25 bps (22-23 bps on AUM basis) with headline NNPA/GNPA of 1.10-1.15% by year-end.
Rate pass-through is undecided: ALCO expected in December/January after the RBI policy, with up to a one-quarter lag; watch whether spreads hold given about 75% floating assets and liabilities.
Competition is rising: industry balance transfer-out is about 6.5-7% versus Aadhar's 5.1%; watch BT-out as it typically rises in Q2 and Q3.
Non-home loan share is targeted to rise from 26% to about 28% by year-end; watch NHL disbursement growth and GNPA (about 2.0%).
Regulatory items pending: IRDAI draft insurance guidelines and any NHB outlay increase, neither quantified yet; branch additions of 40-50 for FY27 with only about 5-6 added so far.
key_quotes: Our approach is to protect spreads rather than chase yields.
We are quite confident of drawing these back and the credit cost back to our 25 basis points as we end the financial year.
There is no circular from NHB as yet on an increased outlay, so I will leave media reports to media.
Right now, it is completely stable.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, asset quality and the year-end credit cost return to 25 bps, but cautious on rates and competition: management says it will protect spreads rather than chase yields. It was noticeably non-committal on Stage 2 drivers, on the NHB outlay and on the IRDAI insurance rules, saying it is waiting for final guidance or circulars.

adds.what: Branch network expansion: 40-50 branches to be added in FY27 (about 5-6 added so far, about 40 in pipeline); network at 632 branches

growth.why: Management maintains 20% AUM and PAT growth medium-term and guides 20%+ disbursement growth in H2 FY27 (minimum 20% in Q3), backed by 40-50 branch additions in FY27 (about 40 in pipeline), an assignment volume of INR2,000-2,050 crore and October run-rate rising to about INR900 crore/month, though no capacity-style numbers are given for disbursement itself.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says it will protect spreads rather than chase yields after the 25 bps repo hike to 5.5%, with ~75% of assets and liabilities floating and pass-through undecided until the Dec/Jan ALCO; Q2 exit spread is 5.73% and credit cost of 31 bps is above the 25 bps FY guide.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Guidance is 40-50 branch additions in FY27 with only 5-6 added so far and about 40 in the pipeline, taking the network from 632 towards the 670-680 range.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides a minimum of 20% disbursement growth in Q3 and 20%+ in H2, with October run-rate up from about INR800 crore to about INR900 crore a month, against Q2 disbursement of INR2,577 crore (+22% YoY).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex or capacity plan beyond branch additions was discussed; utilisation is not a relevant measure for this lender.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Medium-term guidance was only maintained (20% AUM and PAT growth, 18-20% disbursement growth), and Q2 credit cost of 31 bps sits above the 25 bps FY guide with rate and competition headwinds flagged.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Credit cost of 31 bps in Q2 is above the 25 bps annual guide and the company needs to bring it back down by year-end, while Stage 2 rose to about 3.55% from about 3.3% and BT-out is 5.1% against an industry 6.5-7%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or molecule launch was discussed; the only new initiatives are in-house AI platforms with no date or financial scale given.

rows.label: Rate pass-through decision after RBI hike
rows.when: Dec/Jan ALCO, lag up to one quarter
rows.why: Repo rose 25 bps to 5.5% and ~75% of assets and liabilities are floating, with no pass-through decision yet and the ALCO due in Dec/Jan; the rating upgrades are expected to cut NCD costs by about 20 bps, so spreads should hold to a large extent.

rows.label: Cost-to-income improvement
rows.why: ESOP-adjusted cost-to-income fell 230 bps YoY to 33.9% in Q2 and H1 is 34% (-215 bps), and AA+ ratings are opening cheaper funding pools such as pension and life insurers.

rows.label: IRDAI draft insurance guidelines and NHB outlay
rows.why: Both are unquantified: IRDAI draft rules are under industry review (management says fee and opex levers can offset) and there is no NHB circular yet on a larger outlay, though a fresh NHB sanction of INR1,000 crore was received.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, asset quality and the return to 25 bps credit cost by year-end, but cautious on rates and competition and non-committal on Stage 2 drivers, the NHB outlay and IRDAI rules; analysts pressed on Stage 2 rising QoQ and the Q2 credit cost above guidance.
